settings.definition_quote:
While in the main text for simplicity we only consider distributions bounded on the $[0,1]$ interval all proofs relating to the 	bp and \stbp given in the appendix will extend to the sub Gaussian case. The lower bound for the \ctbp will also extend to the sub Gaussian case. That is we redefine the setting as follows: the learner is presented with a $K$-armed bandit problem $\unu =\{
u_1,\ldots,
u_K\}$, where $
u_k$ is the unknown distribution of arm $k$. Let $\sigma^2 >0$, all arms are assumed to be $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian as described in the following definition, we write $\mu_k$ for the mean of arm $k$.

source.label: thm:unstr_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\cB) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{K\log K}{T}}.$$ The algorithm \unif described in Sections~\ref{sec:optimal_alg} attains this rate.

results.notes: Upper half of the minimax Theta statement. Simple regret here is the expected maximal gap of misclassified arms (TBP regret).

source.label: thm:unstr_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\cB) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{K\log K}{T}}.$$

results.notes: Lower half of minimax rate; hard instances are Bernoulli(1/2 +- eps).

conditions: hard instances are Gaussian N(+-eps, sigma^2)

source.label: prop:unstr_lo
source.quote: For any $T\geq 1$ and any strategy $\pi$, there exists a unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \B$, such that \[ \bR^{\pi,\unu}_T \geq \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2 \max\big(2,\log(K)\big) K }{8T}}\,. \]

results.notes: Proved with Gaussian instances; adapts to Bernoulli up to constants.

source.label: prop:unstr_hiprob_up
source.quote: For any unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \cB$, any $T\geq K$, any $0 < \delta < 1$, \unif satisfies $$\mathbb P_{\unu}\left(R_T^{\unif, \unu} \geq \sqrt{\frac{ 4 \sigma^2 K}{T}\log\left(\frac{2 K}{ \delta}\right)}\right) \leq \delta\,.$$

results.notes: Holds simultaneously for all delta; delta is not an algorithm input.

source.label: prop:unstr_exp_up
source.quote: For any unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \cB$, and any $T\geq K$, \unif satisfies $$\bR_T^{\unif, \unu} \leq 7\sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2\log(2K) K}{T}}\;.$$

source.label: thm:mon_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bs) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{T}}.$$ The algorithm \stb described in Section \ref{sec:optimal_alg} attains this rate.

source.label: thm:mon_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bs) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{T}}.$$

conditions: hard instances are Gaussian step functions

source.label: prop:mon_lo
source.quote: For any $T\geq 1$ and any strategy $\pi$, there exists a structured bandit problem $\unu \in \Bs$, such that \[ \bR^{\pi,\unu}_T \geq \frac{1}{8}\sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2 \max\big(2,\log(K)\big)}{8T}}\,. \]

symbols.eps_lvl: regret level epsilon at which the tail probability P(R_T >= epsilon) is evaluated
symbols.epsilon_0: sqrt(2 sigma^2 log(48)/T_2), T_2 = floor(T/(3 ceil(6 log K)))

conditions: problem in the relaxed monotone class B_m^{*,epsilon} (clipped signed gaps increasing), which contains B_m

source.label: prop:mo_hiprob_up
source.quote: For any $\epsilon > \epsilon_0$ and any problem $\unu \in \Bs^{*,\epsilon}$, and any $T > 6 \log(K)$, the \stb Algorithm will achieve the following bound on simple regret, \PP_{\unu}(R_T^{\stb, \unu} \geq \epsilon ) \leq \min( \exp(-\frac{3\log(K)}{4}), 72 \log(K) \exp(-\frac{T\epsilon^2}{216 \sigma^2 \log(K)}) )

results.notes: Bound on the tail probability P(R_T >= eps) of the simple regret, recorded as quantity 'other'. Proof's conclusion gives constant 324 and eps >= 3 eps_0, inconsistent with statement; recorded as stated. Corollary 11 restates it for general increasing clipped sequences.

source.label: cor:mo_exp_up
source.quote: For any problem $\unu \in \Bs$ and any $T \geq 12\log(K)$, the \stb algorithm will achieve the following bound on expected regret, $$\bR^{\stb, \unu}_T \leq 80 \sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2 \log(K)}{T}}\,.$$

results.notes: Paper notes a doubling-trick anytime version holds with T replaced by T/4.

tuning: SR subroutine: any minimax-optimal TOP-1 simple-regret algorithm (e.g. MOSS with randomized recommendation)

source.label: thm:un_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bu) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{K}{T}}.$$ The algorithm \UTB described in Section \ref{sec:optimal_alg} attains this rate.

source.label: thm:un_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bu) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{K}{T}}.$$

conditions: hard instances: one Gaussian arm at eps, others at 0

source.label: prop:unimod_lo
source.quote: For any $T\geq 1$ and any strategy $\pi$, there exists an unimodal bandit problem $\unu \in \Bu$, such that \[ \bR^{\pi,\unu}_T \geq \frac{1}{8}\sqrt{\frac{K}{T}}\,. \]

tuning: SR subroutine: any minimax-optimal TOP-1 simple-regret algorithm

source.label: prop:exp_uni_hi
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $c_{\mathrm{uni}}>0$ such that for any unimodal bandit problem $\unu \in \Bu$, \UTB satisfies $$\bR_T^{\ctb, \unu} \leq c_{\mathrm{uni}}\sqrt{\frac{ K}{n}}\;.$$

results.notes: Statement writes R^{CTB} and n; context indicates UTB and n = T. Universal constant c_uni.

source.label: thm:con_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bc) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{ \loglog K}{T}}.$$ The algorithm \CTB described in Section \ref{sec:optimal_alg} attains this rate.

source.label: thm:con_minmax
source.quote: It holds that $$\bR_T^*(\Bc) \asymp \sqrt{\frac{ \loglog K}{T}}.$$

results.notes: Supporting Proposition 9 requires K >= e^12; Theorem stated without that condition.

source.label: prop:lb_cvx
source.quote: For any $T\geq 1$, $K\geq e^{12}$ and any strategy $\pi$, there exists a structured bandit problem $\unu \in \Bc$, such that \[ \bR^{\pi,\unu}_T \geq \frac{1}{8}\sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2 \max\big(2,\log(\log(K)-1)\big)}{8T}}\,. \]

source.label: prop:exp_con_hi
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $c_{\mathrm{conv}}>0$ such that for any convex bandit problem $\unu \in \Bc$, \CTB satisfies $$\bR_T^{\ctb, \unu} \leq c_{\mathrm{conv}}\sqrt{\frac{\log\log K \lor 1}{T}}\;.$$

conditions: any strategy that stops at a stopping time and is (epsilon, delta)-PAC

source.label: cor:tbppaclb
source.quote: Let $\epsilon, \delta>0$. It holds that for any strategy $\pi$ that stops at a stopping time $\sT^\pi_{\epsilon, \delta}$ and that is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC, there exists a unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \B$, such that \mathbb E_{\unu} [\sT^\pi_{\epsilon, \delta}] \geq \frac{2\sigma^2 K \max(\log(K),2) (1 - K^{-1} - \delta)^2}{\epsilon^2}

conditions: any strategy that stops at a stopping time and is (epsilon, delta)-PAC

source.label: cor:stppaclb
source.quote: Let $\epsilon, \delta>0$ and $K \geq 2 $. It holds that for any strategy $\pi$ that stops at a stopping time $\sT_{\epsilon, \delta}$ and that is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC, there exists a unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \Bs$, such that \mathbb E_{\unu} [\sT_{\epsilon, \delta}] \geq \frac{2\sigma^2 \max(2,\log(K)) (1 - K^{-1} - \delta)^2}{\epsilon^2}

tuning: T := floor(2 sigma^2 K log(2K/delta)/epsilon^2) + K

source.label: cor:tbppac
source.quote: Let $\epsilon, \delta >0$. For any unstructured bandit problem $\unu \in \cB$, Algorithm \unif launched with parameter $T := \lfloor\frac{2 \sigma^2 K \log(2K/\delta)}{\epsilon^2}\rfloor +K$ is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC.

results.notes: Deterministic stopping time; recorded as sample complexity of an (epsilon,delta)-PAC strategy (floor dropped as upper bound).

source.label: cor:stppac
source.quote: For any problem $\unu \in \mathcal{B}_s$, algorithm \stb launched with parameter $T := \lfloor \frac{21\sigma^2 \log(K)}{\epsilon^2} + 12\log(K)\rfloor$ if $\delta \geq K^{-3/4}$ and $T:=\lfloor \frac{432 \sigma^2 \log(K) \log(9/\delta)}{\epsilon^2} + 12\log(K)\rfloor$ otherwise, is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC.

tuning: T := floor(432 sigma^2 log(K) log(9/delta)/epsilon^2 + 12 log(K))

source.label: cor:stppac
source.quote: algorithm \stb launched with parameter ... $T:=\lfloor \frac{432 \sigma^2 \log(K) \log(9/\delta)}{\epsilon^2} + 12\log(K)\rfloor$ otherwise, is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PAC.
